steps.say: Bones cannot move by themselves. Muscles pull on them to move them.
A joint is where two bones meet. Your elbow, knee and shoulder are joints.
Tendons join muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, it gets shorter and pulls the bone.
Muscles can only pull, so they work in pairs. One pulls a bone one way, and the other pulls it back.
To bend your arm, the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes. To straighten it, the triceps contracts.
Elbows and knees are hinge joints. Shoulders and hips are ball-and-socket joints.

check.prompt: Which muscle contracts to bend your arm?

options.why: The tongue helps you eat and talk.

hints: This muscle is on the front of your upper arm.
It bulges when you curl your arm.
It is the partner of the triceps.
check.explanation: The biceps contracts and pulls the lower arm up, so the arm bends.

check.prompt: A muscle can only ___ a bone. It can never push it.
hints: Think about what a shorter muscle does to a bone.
It is the opposite of push.
check.explanation: Muscles pull on bones by contracting. They cannot push.
